Build a one page website for a design agency

I have built a one-page digital flagship website for **ATELIER LUMA** — an independent design practice specializing in brand architecture, digital product systems, and spatial computing.

### 🌐 Live Preview
You can view the live site here:
**[https://antigravity.luch.dev/site/fffaad97-a521-4754-8383-fc4786ced846/404c0102c737056bf40cb973/](https://antigravity.luch.dev/site/fffaad97-a521-4754-8383-fc4786ced846/404c0102c737056bf40cb973/)**

---

### ✨ Key Features & Architecture

1. **Brand Identity & Aesthetic**:
   - **Typography**: Editorial avant-garde pairing using [`Syne`](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Syne) for bold display titles, [`Plus Jakarta Sans`](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Plus+Jakarta+Sans) for body copy, and [`JetBrains Mono`](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/JetBrains+Mono) for metadata, tags, and timestamps.
   - **Dual Visual Themes**: Instant theme toggle between **Dark Obsidian** and **Editorial Light** modes in [`initTheme`](https://github.com/oxNelson/build-a-one-page-website-for/blob/main/js/main.js#L26-L54) with `localStorage` persistence.
   - **Interactive Ambient Canvas**: Fluid organic gradient blobs rendered via 2D Canvas in [`initAmbientCanvas`](https://github.com/oxNelson/build-a-one-page-website-for/blob/main/js/main.js#L59-L135) that gently react to mouse movement.
   - **Micro-Haptics & Audio Synthesizer**: Subtle audio feedback powered natively by the Web Audio API in [`initSoundEffects`](https://github.com/oxNelson/build-a-one-page-website-for/blob/main/js/main.js#L540-L612) (zero external audio file downloads needed).

2. **Hero & Status Bar**:
   - **Live Studio World Clocks**: Synchronized real-time clocks for New York, London, Zurich, and Tokyo in [`initLiveClocks`](https://github.com/oxNelson/build-a-one-page-website-for/blob/main/js/main.js#L187-L215).
   - **Availability Ticker**: Live pulsing badge indicating current studio capacity for Q1/Q2 commissions.
   - **Key Agency Metrics**: 48+ International Design Honors, 140+ Shipped Products, $2.4B Client Valuation Raised, 98.4% Retention.

3. **Partners & Infinite Marquee**:
   - Continuous marquee showcasing category-defining clients (*Polestar, Teenage Engineering, Leica, Stripe, Arc, Sonos, Linear, Bang & Olufsen*).

4. **Curated Portfolio & Interactive Case Study Modal**:
   - Filterable project grid (*Digital Products, Brand Identity, Creative Tech, Spatial & 3D*) in [`initPortfolio`](https://github.com/oxNelson/build-a-one-page-website-for/blob/main/js/main.js#L358-L387).
   - Clickable cards that launch an editorial case study overlay in [`initCaseStudyModal`](https://github.com/oxNelson/build-a-one-page-website-for/blob/main/js/main.js#L392-L474) with challenge statements, strategic solutions, performance metrics, project gallery, and client endorsements.

5. **Interactive Project Scope & Investment Estimator**:
   - Bespoke interactive calculator widget in [`initEstimator`](https://github.com/oxNelson/build-a-one-page-website-for/blob/main/js/main.js#L479-L566) allowing prospective clients to configure discipline, timeline horizon, and team pod depth to receive instant real-time budget brackets and team recommendations.
   - Includes an **"Apply Scope to Project Brief"** action that pre-fills the contact form and smooth-scrolls directly to the inquiry section.

6. **Full Suite of Agency Sections**:
   - **Capabilities & Services**: Accordion breakdown with itemized deliverable tags in [`initServicesAccordion`](https://github.com/oxNelson/build-a-one-page-website-for/blob/main/js/main.js#L571-L585).
   - **Studio Philosophy**: The 3 pillars (*Radical Reduction, Systematic Rigor, Code as Material*).
   - **Methodology Timeline**: 5-phase interactive step roadmap with milestone checklists in [`initProcessTabs`](https://github.com/oxNelson/build-a-one-page-website-for/blob/main/js/main.js#L590-L608).
   - **Awards Shelf & Testimonials**: Industry accolades and client quotes.
   - **FAQ Accordion**: Answers to common client questions regarding IP ownership, tech stack, and engagement models in [`initFaqAccordion`](https://github.com/oxNelson/build-a-one-page-website-for/blob/main/js/main.js#L613-L627).
   - **Project Brief & Inquiry Form**: Client intake form with dynamic validation and generated reference code in [`initContactForm`](https://github.com/oxNelson/build-a-one-page-website-for/blob/main/js/main.js#L632-L666), plus a one-click studio email copy button with toast notifications in [`initEmailCopy`](https://github.com/oxNelson/build-a-one-page-website-for/blob/main/js/main.js#L694-L708).

### 📁 Created Files
- [index.html](https://github.com/oxNelson/build-a-one-page-website-for/blob/main/index.html) — Semantic HTML5 structure and accessible markup
- [css/style.css](https://github.com/oxNelson/build-a-one-page-website-for/blob/main/css/style.css) — Custom properties, typography, glassmorphism, responsive grid & animations
- [js/main.js](https://github.com/oxNelson/build-a-one-page-website-for/blob/main/js/main.js) — Interactive engine, canvas animation, modal, audio synthesis, and calculator
- [README.md](https://github.com/oxNelson/build-a-one-page-website-for/blob/main/README.md) — Documentation and live preview details

SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS SPECIFICATION (SRS)

Obsidian Design Agency — Corporate Website

Project: Obsidian Design Agency Website
Business Location: Nigeria
Project Type: Five-page, responsive design agency website
Deployment Platform: Netlify
Source Code Repository: GitHub
Recommended Technology: React + TypeScript + Vite + Tailwind CSS
Authentication: Not required
Backend: Not required for the initial release
Quality Standard: Production-ready, responsive, accessible, SEO-friendly, and deployment-verified

⸻

1. PROJECT OVERVIEW

1.1 Project Purpose

Design, develop, test, and deploy a modern, premium website for Obsidian Design Agency, a creative design agency operating in Nigeria.

The website must communicate professionalism, creativity, strategic thinking, and trust. It should help potential clients understand the agency’s services, explore its portfolio, learn about the team or brand, and initiate project enquiries.

The finished product must feel like a credible creative agency rather than a generic template.

1.2 Primary Objectives

* Establish a strong and recognizable digital identity for Obsidian Design Agency.
* Present services and creative work in a clear, visually compelling format.
* Generate qualified enquiries from Nigerian and international clients.
* Deliver an excellent mobile, tablet, and desktop experience.
* Achieve strong performance and search engine discoverability.
* Enable simple updates through a GitHub-based workflow.
* Deploy reliably on Netlify with no build errors.
* Avoid unnecessary infrastructure, authentication, databases, and server-side dependencies.

1.3 Target Audience

The website should serve:

* Nigerian startups and small-to-medium businesses.
* Established companies seeking branding or digital design.
* Entrepreneurs launching new products or businesses.
* International clients seeking creative services from a Nigerian agency.
* Organizations requiring websites, brand identities, marketing materials, or digital experiences.

⸻

2. SCOPE OF THE WEBSITE

The website must contain exactly five primary pages.

No.	Page	Route	Purpose
1	Home	/	Introduce the agency and convert visitors
2	About	/about	Explain the agency’s identity, values, and approach
3	Services	/services	Present creative and digital services
4	Portfolio	/portfolio	Showcase selected projects and case studies
5	Contact	/contact	Enable visitors to enquire about projects

The navigation must be consistent across all five pages.

The website must not contain login, sign-up, account registration, user dashboards, or password recovery pages.

A contact form is permitted, but it must not require visitors to create an account.

⸻

3. FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS

3.1 Page One — Home

Route: /

The homepage must communicate the agency’s value proposition immediately.

Required sections:

1. Header with logo, navigation, and a prominent contact CTA.
2. Hero section featuring a compelling headline, supporting text, and primary CTA.
3. Selected portfolio projects or featured work.
4. Overview of the agency’s core services.
5. Brief introduction to the agency’s approach.
6. A process or methodology section explaining how projects are delivered.
7. Client testimonials, only where genuine testimonials are available.
8. Strong project enquiry CTA.
9. Footer with contact details, navigation, social links, and copyright information.

Suggested headline direction:

“Bold Ideas. Distinctive Design. Brands Built to Stand Out.”

The content must position Obsidian as a strategic creative partner rather than simply a provider of graphic design.

Primary CTA: Start a Project

Secondary CTA: Explore Our Work

3.2 Page Two — About

Route: /about

Required sections:

* Agency introduction and background.
* Mission and vision.
* Design philosophy and creative values.
* Approach to solving business and communication problems.
* Project collaboration process.
* Team or founder introduction, if verified information is supplied.
* CTA linking to the contact page.

Do not invent staff names, qualifications, client relationships, awards, or years of experience. Use editable placeholders until the agency supplies accurate information.

3.3 Page Three — Services

Route: /services

The services page must explain what the agency offers, what each service delivers, and how clients can enquire.

Recommended service categories:

* Brand identity and strategy.
* Logo design and visual identity systems.
* Website design and development.
* UI/UX and digital product design.
* Graphic design and marketing collateral.
* Social media creative design.
* Packaging and print design, where offered.

Each service must include:

* Service name.
* Short, benefit-oriented description.
* Deliverables or scope.
* Relevant visual element or project example.
* CTA linking to the contact page.

Only advertise services the agency intends to provide. Service content must be easy to update from a centralized data file.

Do not display fabricated pricing or unsupported guarantees.

3.4 Page Four — Portfolio

Route: /portfolio

The portfolio must demonstrate the agency’s creative capabilities and quality of execution.

Required features:

* Responsive project gallery.
* Project thumbnail, title, category, and short description.
* Optional category filters.
* Dedicated project detail views or expandable project details within the same portfolio route.
* Project challenges, design approach, and outcomes where documented.
* CTA inviting visitors to commission similar work.

Suggested categories include branding, digital design, web design, and marketing design.

Portfolio data must be managed through a centralized TypeScript or JSON-compatible data structure.

Use only original work, authorized imagery, or properly licensed assets. If real projects are unavailable, use clearly labeled concept projects rather than presenting fictional client work as genuine.

3.5 Page Five — Contact

Route: /contact

Required sections:

* Short, welcoming contact introduction.
* Contact form.
* Business email, telephone number, and social links when supplied.
* Nigerian location or service area, if confirmed.
* Expected response-time statement only if the agency can support it.
* Optional project enquiry guidance.

Contact form fields:

* Full name.
* Email address.
* Company or brand name, optional.
* Service required.
* Estimated budget, optional.
* Project description.
* Consent checkbox where appropriate.

Requirements:

* Validate required fields and email format.
* Provide clear validation messages.
* Prevent submission when required fields are invalid.
* Display an understandable success or failure message.
* Protect against accidental duplicate submissions.
* Do not falsely report a successful submission if the message was not delivered.

Contact form implementation: Use a compatible Netlify Forms configuration or an explicitly configured third-party form endpoint. For Netlify Forms, implement the required HTML form attributes and ensure the form is discoverable during the production build. Test actual submission on the deployed site.

The frontend must not expose secret API keys or credentials.

⸻

4. DESIGN AND USER EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS

4.1 Visual Direction

The website should use a premium, contemporary, editorial design language.

Suggested art direction:

* Obsidian-inspired dark tones.
* Off-white or warm neutral backgrounds.
* A restrained accent color such as muted gold, silver, or electric violet.
* Strong typography and generous whitespace.
* High-quality imagery and project mockups.
* Consistent spacing, alignment, and visual hierarchy.
* Subtle transitions and restrained motion.
* Clear, high-contrast calls to action.

The design must remain readable and usable. Avoid excessive animations, unnecessary gradients, generic stock imagery, and overly decorative layouts.

4.2 Responsive Design

Support these viewport ranges:

* Mobile: 320–767 px.
* Tablet: 768–1023 px.
* Desktop: 1024 px and above.

Requirements:

* No horizontal overflow at supported viewport sizes.
* Mobile navigation must be functional and keyboard accessible.
* Images must scale without distortion.
* Text must remain legible on small screens.
* Forms and buttons must be easy to operate by touch.
* Layouts must adapt rather than merely shrink.

4.3 Accessibility

Target WCAG 2.2 Level AA where practical.

Implement:

* Semantic HTML landmarks.
* Keyboard-accessible navigation and controls.
* Visible keyboard focus.
* Accessible form labels and error messages.
* Appropriate image alternative text.
* Sufficient text contrast.
* Reduced-motion support.
* Logical heading hierarchy.

4.4 Interaction Quality

Every visible interactive element must perform a real action.

Examples:

* Navigation links must open the correct page.
* CTA buttons must navigate to a valid destination.
* Portfolio filters must filter projects if presented as functional filters.
* Mobile menu controls must open and close the menu.
* Social links must point to valid destinations.
* Form buttons must validate or submit the form.

Do not include decorative buttons that do nothing or placeholder links such as href="#".

⸻

5. TECHNICAL ARCHITECTURE

5.1 Required Technology Stack

Component	Requirement
Frontend	React
Language	TypeScript with strict checking
Build tool	Vite
Styling	Tailwind CSS
Routing	React Router, or an equally reliable explicit routing solution
Icons	Lucide React or another maintained icon library
Form handling	Native validation and Netlify Forms or a configured external endpoint
Version control	Git and GitHub
Hosting	Netlify
Content	Local TypeScript/JSON data
Database	Not required
Authentication	Not required

Use mutually compatible, stable package versions and commit the package lockfile.

Do not install multiple libraries that solve the same problem without a clear reason.

5.2 Recommended Project Structure

obsidian-design-agency/
├── public/
│   ├── favicon.svg
│   ├── images/
│   ├── robots.txt
│   └── _redirects
├── src/
│   ├── assets/
│   ├── components/
│   │   ├── Navbar.tsx
│   │   ├── Footer.tsx
│   │   ├── Button.tsx
│   │   ├── SectionHeading.tsx
│   │   └── ProjectCard.tsx
│   ├── data/
│   │   ├── services.ts
│   │   └── projects.ts
│   ├── layouts/
│   │   └── MainLayout.tsx
│   ├── pages/
│   │   ├── Home.tsx
│   │   ├── About.tsx
│   │   ├── Services.tsx
│   │   ├── Portfolio.tsx
│   │   └── Contact.tsx
│   ├── App.tsx
│   ├── main.tsx
│   └── index.css
├── index.html
├── package.json
├── package-lock.json
├── tsconfig.json
├── vite.config.ts
├── netlify.toml
├── .gitignore
└── README.md

This structure is a reference architecture. The final implementation may vary, provided that it remains organized, maintainable, and deployable.

⸻

6. BUILD AND DEPLOYMENT REQUIREMENTS

This section is mandatory. Deployment reliability takes priority over unnecessary technical complexity.

6.1 Build Configuration

The project must:

* Install from the committed lockfile.
* Use a supported Node.js LTS version.
* Run successfully using the documented build command.
* Produce the production site in the dist directory.
* Avoid relying on files outside the repository.
* Avoid environment-specific absolute file paths.
* Avoid missing imports and unresolved dependencies.
* Avoid case-sensitive filename mismatches.
* Avoid committing secrets or private credentials.

Use TypeScript strict mode and correct all actual TypeScript errors.

Do not suppress errors broadly or disable checks just to obtain a successful build.

6.2 Required package scripts

The package configuration must expose working scripts equivalent to:

{
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "vite",
    "build": "tsc -b && vite build",
    "preview": "vite preview"
  }
}

Adjust the TypeScript build command if the chosen Vite/TypeScript template uses a different valid project-reference setup. The final command must work with the actual committed configuration.

The build must exit with status code 0.

6.3 Netlify Configuration

Configure the project explicitly for Netlify.

Example netlify.toml:

[build]
  command = "npm run build"
  publish = "dist"
[[redirects]]
  from = "/*"
  to = "/index.html"
  status = 200

This configuration is appropriate for a client-side React Router application. If using a different routing architecture, adjust the fallback accordingly and verify that all five routes work on direct navigation and refresh.

Do not duplicate or contradict the routing fallback in multiple configuration files. Choose one clear, tested configuration.

6.4 Node.js and Dependency Management

* Pin the supported Node.js major version through .nvmrc or a documented equivalent.
* Ensure the Node.js version used locally matches the intended Netlify build environment.
* Commit package-lock.json.
* Use npm ci in clean-install verification.
* Resolve peer dependency conflicts properly.
* Do not rely on npm install --force or npm install --legacy-peer-deps as a substitute for resolving incompatible packages.
* Remove unused dependencies.
* Do not leave imports pointing to missing files.

6.5 GitHub Integration

The repository must contain all source code and configuration required to build the website.

Requirements:

* Initialize Git and commit the complete project.
* Push the project to the designated GitHub repository.
* Connect that repository to Netlify.
* Configure the production branch, normally main.
* Enable automatic deployment when changes are pushed.
* Verify that the latest commit is the one deployed.
* Document the deployment and recovery process in the README.

Do not commit .env files containing secrets, node_modules, or local build artifacts unless there is a specific justified reason.

6.6 Environment Variables

The initial website should not require environment variables unless a real integration needs them.

If variables are required:

* Document each variable in .env.example.
* Configure production values through Netlify’s environment variable settings.
* Never commit actual secrets.
* Ensure missing optional integrations do not crash unrelated pages.

6.7 Asset Reliability

* Use valid, available image assets.
* Prefer optimized local assets for critical branding and portfolio imagery.
* Use appropriately sized WebP, AVIF, or other supported formats where beneficial.
* Avoid broken remote image URLs and unlicensed assets.
* Add appropriate image dimensions to minimize layout shifts.
* Do not make the entire site dependent on a third-party image service.
* Ensure fonts have reliable fallback options.

⸻

7. QUALITY ASSURANCE AND TESTING

Testing must be performed before the project is declared complete.

7.1 Clean Build Test

Execute these commands from a fresh checkout:

npm ci
npm run build
npm run preview

Confirm that:

* Dependencies install successfully.
* TypeScript checks pass.
* Vite generates the production bundle.
* The preview server starts correctly.
* The generated site loads without fatal console errors.

7.2 Page and Routing Test

Verify all five routes:

* /
* /about
* /services
* /portfolio
* /contact

For each route:

* Open it directly in a new browser tab.
* Refresh the page.
* Navigate to it through the website menu.
* Confirm that the correct content loads.
* Confirm that there are no blank pages or JavaScript runtime errors.

Also verify unknown routes produce a sensible not-found experience rather than silently displaying an unrelated page.

7.3 Responsive Test

Test the website at representative mobile, tablet, and desktop widths.

Verify:

* Navigation.
* Layout and spacing.
* Typography.
* Portfolio grids.
* Image behavior.
* Form usability.
* Footer layout.
* Absence of horizontal overflow.

7.4 Functional Test

Verify every CTA, navigation item, filter, menu control, form validation state, and external link.

For the contact form, test both valid and invalid submissions on the deployed site. Confirm that a valid submission reaches the intended destination.

7.5 Production Test

After deploying to Netlify:

* Open the production URL.
* Test all five pages.
* Refresh nested routes.
* Check the browser console and network errors.
* Inspect Netlify build logs.
* Verify image loading.
* Confirm HTTPS is enabled.
* Confirm the production deployment uses the intended GitHub commit.
* Submit a real test enquiry and verify delivery.

Do not mark deployment as successful based only on a local build.

⸻

8. PERFORMANCE, SEO, AND SECURITY

8.1 Performance

Optimize for good Core Web Vitals.

Targets under representative testing conditions:

* Largest Contentful Paint: 2.5 seconds or less.
* Interaction to Next Paint: 200 milliseconds or less.
* Cumulative Layout Shift: 0.1 or less.

Use Lighthouse to evaluate performance, accessibility, SEO, and best practices. Treat these as targets to verify, not guaranteed results.

Implementation requirements:

* Minimize unnecessary JavaScript.
* Lazy-load below-the-fold images where appropriate.
* Avoid oversized video backgrounds.
* Optimize fonts and image delivery.
* Use route-level code splitting if justified.
* Avoid expensive animations and unnecessary dependencies.

8.2 SEO

Each page must include:

* A unique page title.
* A relevant meta description.
* A canonical URL once the production domain is known.
* A logical heading hierarchy.
* Descriptive image alt text.
* Open Graph metadata.
* Appropriate social sharing metadata.

Also provide:

* A favicon.
* robots.txt.
* An XML sitemap for the production domain.
* Descriptive page URLs.
* Local business structured data only when the agency’s details are verified.

Do not invent a street address, business telephone number, social profile, or Google Business Profile.

8.3 Security and Privacy

* Do not collect unnecessary personal data.
* Do not expose API keys in frontend code.
* Use HTTPS in production.
* Validate form submissions and implement reasonable spam prevention.
* Do not introduce third-party tracking without a defined requirement.
* Include a privacy notice if personal data is collected.
* Do not implement authentication, user accounts, or a database unless the project scope changes.

⸻

9. CONTENT AND BRAND ASSETS

Before launch, the agency should supply:

* Official logo and any brand guidelines.
* Brand colors and preferred typography, if established.
* Verified agency description.
* Confirmed service list.
* Real portfolio projects and authorized imagery.
* Official contact email and telephone number.
* Social media profile URLs.
* Production domain, if available.
* Genuine testimonials, if available.
* Privacy information appropriate to the deployed contact form.

When information is missing, use clearly marked editable placeholders in development.

Never invent client logos, testimonials, awards, company registration claims, or measurable business results.

The site must remain complete and visually coherent even if optional testimonials or team photographs are unavailable.

⸻

10. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

The project is complete only when all mandatory criteria below have been satisfied.

* [ ]	Exactly five primary pages are implemented.
* [ ]	No login, sign-up, or account dashboard exists.
* [ ]	All five pages use a consistent navigation and footer.
* [ ]	The design works on mobile, tablet, and desktop.
* [ ]	All visible interactive elements work.
* [ ]	The contact form has a real, tested delivery mechanism.
* [ ]	All production images and links work.
* [ ]	The project builds successfully from a clean checkout.
* [ ]	TypeScript and production build checks pass.
* [ ]	The package lockfile is committed.
* [ ]	Netlify uses the correct build command and publish directory.
* [ ]	Direct navigation and refresh work on all five routes.
* [ ]	The deployed website has no critical console errors.
* [ ]	HTTPS is enabled.
* [ ]	Page metadata and essential SEO files are present.
* [ ]	The GitHub repository is connected to Netlify.
* [ ]	Automatic deployments from the production branch work.
* [ ]	The final production URL has been tested.
* [ ]	Setup and deployment instructions are documented in the README.

A checkbox may be marked complete only after the relevant result has been verified.

⸻

11. REQUIRED DELIVERABLES

The developer or AI coding agent must provide:

1. Complete, working source code.
2. The full five-page responsive website.
3. Reusable components and organized content data.
4. All necessary build and deployment configuration files.
5. A committed dependency lockfile.
6. A working contact form integration.
7. Essential SEO assets and metadata.
8. A README containing installation, development, build, and deployment instructions.
9. A concise QA report listing the checks performed and their results.
10. A GitHub repository URL.
11. A Netlify production URL, once deployment is completed.

If deployment cannot be completed because credentials, repository permissions, or domain access are unavailable, clearly identify the blocker. Do not claim the site has been deployed without verification.

⸻

12. MASTER IMPLEMENTATION INSTRUCTION

Build the Obsidian Design Agency website according to this specification.

Work as a senior frontend engineer, UI/UX designer, and deployment engineer. Prioritize visual quality, maintainable architecture, accessibility, and a verifiable production build.

Follow this implementation sequence:

Phase 1 — Foundation

* Initialize the project.
* Establish the design system.
* Install compatible dependencies.
* Configure TypeScript, Vite, and Tailwind CSS.
* Verify the initial build.

Phase 2 — Development

* Build the shared navigation, footer, layout, and reusable components.
* Implement all five pages.
* Add responsive styling and real interactions.
* Implement and configure the contact form.
* Add SEO metadata and optimized assets.

Phase 3 — Verification

* Run a clean dependency installation.
* Run the production build.
* Resolve every actual build error.
* Test page routing, forms, responsiveness, and interactions.
* Inspect the production preview and browser console.
* Repeat failed tests until they pass.

Phase 4 — Deployment

* Commit all required source and configuration files.
* Push to GitHub.
* Connect the repository to Netlify.
* Verify the production build logs.
* Test all five routes on the live website.
* Verify contact form delivery and direct page refreshes.
* Report the final deployment URL and actual QA results.

Non-negotiable engineering rules

* Do not leave unfinished pages or broken links.
* Do not use fake form success messages.
* Do not suppress genuine compiler errors to force a build.
* Do not depend on files that exist only on the developer’s machine.
* Do not use incompatible or unverified package configurations.
* Do not claim tests passed unless they were executed.
* Do not claim successful deployment unless the production URL has been verified.

Final definition of done: A polished, fully functional five-page Obsidian Design Agency website that builds from a clean GitHub checkout, deploys successfully to Netlify, and works correctly on the production URL.

I am currently installing the foundational dependencies (`react`, `react-dom`, `react-router-dom`, `lucide-react`, `vite`, `typescript`, and `tailwindcss`) to build the 5-page **Obsidian Design Agency** website. I will proceed with configuration and implementation as soon as installation completes.
